chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

A man accused a Magian man in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Hush!' The man said: 'He marries his mother or his sister.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is a marriage among them in their religion.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say about a Magian man marrying his mother or sister?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, a man reports to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) that a Magian married his mother or sister, prompting the Imam to clarify that this was a valid custom within their own religious law (*din*). This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of *al-ahwal al-shakhsiyya* (personal status laws), where non-Muslims are judged by their own religious norms regarding marriage validity, rather than Islamic prohibitions. The Imam’s concise response underscores the recognition of *ahl al-dhimma*’s internal legal autonomy in matters of family law.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘A man accused a Magian man in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> so he<sup>asws</sup> said: Muh! (Shh!)’. So the man said, ‘(but) He marries his own mother or his sister’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is a marriage among them in their Religion’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from ‘ Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “

A man once accused a Zoroastrian man before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, he (the Imam) said, ‘Hold it.’ The man said, ‘He marries his mother or sister.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is marriage among them in their religion.’”
